subject.title: [Bug]:  [Windows] exec spawn: all commands hang with no output (stdio pipe deadlock)

question: Should this issue wait for native Windows reproduction before any fix PR is queued?
rationale: Current source and mocked Windows tests show adjacent hardening, but they do not prove the reported all-command no-output timeout is fixed or identify the exact failing path.

options.title: Require native Windows proof first
options.body: Keep the issue open and gather a native Windows gateway trace before any repair PR is queued.

options.title: Queue speculative process hardening
options.body: Allow a fix PR from current source hypotheses, accepting that it may miss the reporter's actual failure mode.

options.title: Wait for reporter evidence
options.body: Leave the issue stale until the reporter adds logs or a recording, reducing maintainer effort but risking an unresolved Windows exec blocker.

recommendation.title: Require native Windows proof first
recommendation.body: Keep the issue open and gather a native Windows gateway trace before any repair PR is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: Current-main blame and recent subprocess hardening make this the best available owner for deciding whether proof is sufficient to queue repair.
